translationRepairs: Li Xian, styled Xianhe, came from Chengji in Longxi.
Li Xian, styled Xianhe; his ancestors were men of Chengji in Longxi.
其先 marks ancestral origin; the original makes Li Xian himself a native of Chengji, against the following settlement at Gaoping.

At the end of Western Wei's Datong era, because the Xian brothers had won great distinction, their forebears were posthumously honored as Governors of Jing, Yuan, and Dongqin provinces and as Minister of Works.

At the end of Western Wei's Datong era, because the Xian brothers had won great distinction, their father was posthumously honored as Governor of Jing, Yuan, and Dongqin provinces and as Minister of Works.
After 父文保，早卒, the silent subject of 追贈 is the father, not plural forebears.
At the end of Western Wei Datong, because the Xian brothers had distinguished merit, posthumously enfeoffed as Governor of Jing, Yuan, and Dongqin provinces and Minister of Works.

At the end of Western Wei Datong, because the Xian brothers had distinguished merit, their father was posthumously granted the offices of Governor of Jing, Yuan, and Dongqin provinces and Minister of Works.
追贈 is a posthumous office grant to the father of s0005, not an enfeoffment; the proposal still reads awkwardly without naming the offices granted.
During Western Wei's Yong'an era, Moqi Chounu rebelled and seized Qi, Jing, and neighboring provinces; Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei sent Erzhu Tianguang to crush him.
During Northern Wei's Yong'an era, Moqi Chounu rebelled and seized Qi, Jing, and neighboring provinces; Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei sent Erzhu Tianguang to crush him.
永安 under 魏孝莊 is a Northern Wei reign (AD 528–530); Western Wei did not yet exist.
As the main force neared Qin Province, Yue abandoned the city and fled. Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent his grandnephew Dao in pursuit with Li Xian as vanguard.
As the main force neared Qin Province, Yue abandoned the city and fled. Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent his nephew Dao in pursuit with Li Xian as vanguard.
兄子導 is Yuwen Tai’s brother’s son (nephew) Dao, not a grandnephew.
When the grand army was about to reach Qin Province, Yue abandoned the city and fled; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered his nephew's son Dao to lead troops in pursuit, with Xian as vanguard.
When the grand army was about to reach Qin Province, Yue abandoned the city and fled; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered his brother's son Dao to lead troops in pursuit, with Xian as vanguard.
兄子 means brother’s son, not a nephew’s son.
Ning did not follow and repeatedly fought and frequently lost northward.
Ning did not follow and repeatedly fought and frequently suffered defeat.
頻北 uses 北 ‘to be defeated’; it is not a northward movement.
He again comforted and reassured Zhangye and the other five commanderies and returned.
He again comforted and reassured Zhangye and the rest of the five commanderies and returned.
張掖等五郡 is five commanderies including Zhangye, not Zhangye plus five more; the proposal’s ‘among the five’ is awkward and needlessly changes 又 from ‘again’ to ‘then’.
While Emperor Gaozu and Prince of Qi Yuwen Hu were still infants, taboo made it inauspicious for them to remain in the palace.
While Emperor Gaozu and Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian were still infants, taboo made it inauspicious for them to remain in the palace.
齊王憲 is Prince of Qi Xian (憲), not Yuwen Hu (護).
When Emperor Gaozu and Prince of Qi Yuwen Hu were still in swaddling clothes, to avoid taboo it was inauspicious for them to live in the palace.
When Emperor Gaozu and Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian were still in swaddling clothes, to avoid taboo it was inauspicious for them to live in the palace.
齊王憲 names Yuwen Xian; substituting Yuwen Hu is a false identification.
Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had them lodged at Yu Xian's household; only after six years did they return to the palace.
Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had them lodged at Xian's household; only after six years did they return to the palace.
于賢家 is the preposition 于 plus Li Xian’s household; 于 is not a surname Yu.
Rebel factions seized the moment and spread their poison.
The Hun faction seized the moment and spread their poison.
匈黨 specifies a Hun/Xiongnu faction; generic ‘rebel factions’ drops that label.
Later, for his service under Houmochen Chong, he was transferred to Administrator of Gaoping.
Later, for merit in answering Houmochen Chong, he was transferred to Administrator of Gaoping.
應侯莫陳崇功 is merit for answering Houmochen Chong’s rising, not service under him.
At Shayuan Li Yuan's merit ranked first; he was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Three Departments, and raised to Duke of Yangping with a fief of three thousand households.
At Shayuan, Li Yuan's merit ranked first; he was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Three Departments, and raised to Duke of Yangping with a fief of three thousand households.
Without the comma, Shayuan can be read as fused with Li Yuan; 沙苑之役 is the battle-place, then 遠.
He was summoned as attendant-in-ordinary, grand general of rapid cavalry, and opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol.
He was summoned as Palace Attendant, Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, and Opening Office with Equal-to-Three-Ministers honors.
侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司 are standard offices; the calque ‘opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol’ is unintelligible.
At that time Gao Huan had encamped at Hene.
At that time Gao Huan had encamped at Heyang.
河陽 is Heyang, not Hene (河內).
At that time Qi Divine Warrior Gao Huan had encamped his troops at Hene.
At that time Qi Divine Warrior Gao Huan had encamped his troops at Heyang.
河陽 is Heyang, not Hene.
Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was pleased and said: "What Li Wan Sui has said is rather to my liking."
Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was pleased and said: "What Li Wansui has said is rather to my liking."
李萬歲 is the courtesy name Wansui, not three separate English words.
The Grand Progenitor was pleased and said: "What Li Wan Sui has said is rather to one's liking."
The Grand Progenitor was pleased and said: "What Li Wansui has said is rather to one's liking."
李萬歲 should be transcribed as Li Wansui.
Before long, he was removed and made left vice director of the secretariat.
Before long, he was appointed left vice director of the secretariat.
除尚書左僕射 uses 除 ‘to appoint’, not ‘to remove’.

The Duke of Lüeyang should be heir apparent—what doubt has Your Grace?
畧陽公 is the ducal title only; the given name Jue is not in this sentence.
Duke Jue of Lueyang should be heir apparent—what doubt has Your Grace?

Later, because of his father's merit, he was enfeoffed Duke of Jian'an county with a fief of one thousand households.
建安縣公 is Duke of Jian’an county, not Jiang’an.
Because his patron had status and because his paternal uncle Li Mu pleaded for him, he was spared.
Because his consort was of high rank and because his paternal uncle Li Mu pleaded for him, he was spared.
主貴 refers to the rank of his princess-consort (義歸公主), not a generic patron.

李賢和兄弟 is Li Xian and his brothers; 和 is the conjunction, not the courtesy name 賢和 fused as Li Xianhe.
